scene.speaker: valentina
scene.bubble: Class records day! The fastest runner, the best singer, the funniest joke… everyone wins at something!
scene.intro: Class records day! Who is the fastest runner? Mateo, easily. Who is the best singer? Valentina, and everybody agrees. Who has got the biggest lunchbox? Mateo again. Who is the funniest? Erik, but he doesn't want to be. They write every record on the wall with a golden star. Who is the tallest in YOUR class? Find your records and write them down!

activities.title: Match the record with the winner.

items.sentence: The blue whale is ___ animal in the world.
Monday is ___ day of the week. So hard!
My grandma is ___ person in our family.
That was ___ joke ever! Ha ha!
Our baby cousin is ___ in the house.

activities.title: Listen to the records ceremony. Write a word or number in each gap.

data.script: Valentina: Class records ceremony! First: the fastest runner… Sofia, with eight seconds! … Mateo: The best drawing of the year goes to Pedro, for his dragon with three heads. … Valentina: The biggest smile award: Mateo! He smiled in every photo of the year. … Mateo: It's true. Even in the dentist photo! … Valentina: The quietest reader: Ana — she read forty books this year. … Mateo: And the special prize: Luna, the best dog assistant in school history! … Valentina: Congratulations, everyone! Now: the biggest cake of the year!

data.text: Create 4 fun class records with your partner (the best laugh, the tidiest pencil case…) and decide together who wins each — with a reason!

activities.title: Two pictures, many differences!
activities.instructions: Look at picture A and picture B. Find the 12 differences and tell your partner about them.

homework.prompt: Write the records of your family: the oldest, the youngest, the funniest, the best cook. One sentence each with because.

outcomes.puede: Understand longer dialogues (Movers parts 1–5); identify specific info in spoken texts.
Describe places, objects, past events; role-play simple situations.
Read and sequence short stories; locate information in signs, notices.
Write a note/message of 30–40 words (Movers Writing part); classroom paragraphs 60–100w.
~1350 words (Movers wordlist); Past simple, relatives, infinitive of purpose, have to.
